properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 17 at 9:21AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County.

.Recent extreme rainfall over the headwaters of the St. Johns River
has caused the river near Cocoa to rise to Major Flood Stage. The
river is forecast to continue to remain steady with slight deviations
in river levels through mid to late week due to additional forecast
heavy rainfall.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa 9w...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 17.2 feet, Water enters homes along the St Johns River
in the Lake Poinsett area west of Cocoa, also low lying homes in
the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park
area of Cocoa. Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes
impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass
Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage
Fish Camp.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:15 AM EST Tuesday the stage was 17.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:15 AM EST Tuesday was 17.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 17.1 to 17.2 feet.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1100 PM EST.

properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued November 17 at 7:58PM EST until November 17 at 9:00PM EST by NWS Key West FL
properties.description:
SMWKEY

The National Weather Service in Key West has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Hawk Channel and Straits of Florida from west end of Seven Mile
Bridge to Halfmoon Shoal out 20 nm...
Gulf Waters from East Cape Sable to Chokoloskee 20 to 60 nm out and
beyond 5 fathoms...
Gulf of America from west end of Seven Mile Bridge to Halfmoon
Shoal out to 5 fathoms...

* Until 900 PM EST.

* At 758 PM EST, severe thunderstorms with possible waterspouts were
located along a line extending from 8 nm north of Ellis Rock Light
to 6 nm east of Halfmoon Shoal Light, moving south at 5 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts, wind gusts 34 knots or greater, and large
hail.

SOURCE...National Weather Service Meteorologist.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can quickly form and capsize boats, cause
considerable damage to vessels and create suddenly higher
waves. Expect wind gusts in excess of 34 knots, suddenly
higher waves, frequent lightning, and heavy downpours.
Large hail could result in injury and damage to boats.

* Locations in the warning include...
Ellis Rock Light, New Ground Rocks Light, and Marquesas Keys.
properties.instruction:
Boaters should seek safe harbor as quickly, and as safely as
possible. When downpours reduce visibility, slow down.

properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued November 17 at 8:01PM EST until November 17 at 9:00PM EST by NWS Miami FL
properties.description:
SMWMFL

The National Weather Service in Miami has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Biscayne Bay...
Coastal waters from Deerfield Beach to Ocean Reef FL out 20 NM...
Coastal waters from Jupiter Inlet to Deerfield Beach FL out 20
NM...

* Until 900 PM EST.

* At 801 PM EST, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located 7 nm east of Port Everglades, or 7 nm
southeast of Lauderdale-By-The-Sea, moving west at 15 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

* Locations impacted include...
Sunny Isles, Lauderdale-By-The-Sea, Hallandale, Fort Lauderdale,
Lighthouse Point, Hillsboro Beach, Bay Harbor Islands, Port
Everglades, Sea Ranch Lakes, Bal Harbour, Golden Beach, Surfside,
Indian Creek, Pompano Beach, Hollywood, Deerfield Beach, Boca
Raton, and Miami Beach.
properties.instruction:
Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.

Report severe weather to the Coast Guard or the National Weather
Service. You can also share your report with NWS Miami on Facebook
and Twitter.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 17 at 5:40PM MST until November 17 at 11:15PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Munds Canyon and Oak Creek near Sedona.

* WHEN...Until 1115 PM MST.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of creeks and normally dry washes is occurring.
Deadly flooding over low-water crossings.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 532 PM MST, river gauges at Munds Canyon and Oak Creek near
Sedona have both crested. However, water levels will remain
elevated over the next few hours as water gradually decreases.
- This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Oak Creek and Dry Beaver Creek.
- For Oak Creek at Sedona:
At 4:45pm the stage was 8.23 feet.
Flood Stage is 14.0 feet.
Forecast: A crest of 8.43 feet is expected by 7:00pm Tuesday.
Impacts:
At 5.0 feet: Multiple private low water crossings and bridges
over Oak Creek above Sedona become impassable.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Sedona, Munds Park, Indian Gardens, Uptown Sedona, Red Rock State
Park and Cathedral Rock.
- This includes the following swimming holes...
Midgely Bridge, Buddha Beach "Red Rock Crossing" and Crescent
Moon Ranch.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:
Stay away or be swept away! The banks of creeks and washes are
unstable and unsafe during any flooding event.

Low water crossings will be dangerous. Do not attempt to cross
flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 17 at 9:19AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.On the St Johns River at Astor, slight rises within Minor Flood
Stage are forecast through at least midweek due to a combination of
northerly winds and water from upstream heavy rainfall working north
through the basin. Rises to Moderate Flood Stage are forecast later
in the week due to the additional heavy rainfall expected.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Minor to Moderate
flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on
or near Wildhog, Bonnet and Snail roads become inaccessible with
several inches of water inside homes along the river and canals.
Docks at Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely
submerged. Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with
yards completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads
flooded in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on
Juno Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EST Tuesday the stage was 2.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 AM EST Tuesday was 2.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 3.4 feet Sunday
morning. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 17 at 7:53PM EST until November 17 at 10:00PM EST by NWS Miami FL
properties.description:
FFWMFL

The National Weather Service in Miami has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northern Broward County in southeastern Florida...

* Until 1000 PM EST.

* At 753 PM EST, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 2 and 4 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Coral Springs, Tamarac, Margate, Lauderhill, Coconut Creek, North
Lauderdale, Lauderdale Lakes, Parkland, Broadview-Pompano Park,
Godfrey Road, Village Park, Palm Aire and Ramblewood East.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 17 at 5:20PM MST until November 17 at 9:15PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
At 520 PM MST, a rise of 6 feet has occurred upstream of Page Springs
at Sedona. The guage at Cornville has begun to rise, with a further
rise expected in the next few hours. Flash flooding is already
occurring.

Flash flooding is expected to begin along Oak Creek in the Page
Springs area within the next few hours.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding.

SOURCE...River gauge reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of Oak Creek.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Cornville, Jordan, Page Springs and Bignotti.

For Oak Creek at Cornville:
At 5:00pm the stage was 2.01 feet.
Flood Stage is 8.0 feet.
Forecast: A crest of 9.17 feet is expected at 9:00pm Tuesday.
Impacts:
At 7.0 feet: Flooding begins to inundate lower terrace of RV park
upstream of Page Springs Road Bridge.
At 8.0 feet: Flooding of lower terrace of RV park upstream of Page
Springs Road Bridge.
At 9.0 feet: Hiking trails along banks of creek affected. Portions of
residential yards flooded.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
Windmill Park.

This includes the following swimming holes...
Mormons Crossing.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Oak Creek.
properties.instruction:
Move to higher ground now. Act quickly to protect your life.

Stay away or be swept away! The banks of creeks and washes are
unstable and unsafe during any flooding event.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.
